tagline: Up the North Fork Toutle into the 1980 blast zone.
intro: SR 504 leaves I-5 at Castle Rock, climbs into the hills above Salmon Creek past farms, and runs along the north side of Silver Lake to Toutle, where the river's two forks meet. Then it follows the North Fork Toutle up its narrowing valley through Kid Valley and past the Toutle River Sediment Dam, climbing through cuts in the cliffs, and beyond Elk Rock it hairpins between viewpoints to Coldwater Lake.

Cowlitz County finished the first road in 1903, to the shore of Spirit Lake. The eruption of May 18, 1980, and its lahar destroyed a major section, and the state rebuilt most of the highway from 1988 to 1997 on a line farther north.

moments.title: Kid Valley
moments.text: Its bridge of 1965 over the North Fork was the only one on the highway that the 1980 mudflows neither damaged nor carried away, because it sat high enough to clear them.

moments.title: Hoffstadt Creek Bridge
moments.text: The longest of the highway's 13 bridges runs 2,340 feet, 370 feet above the valley floor, and marks the western edge of the blast zone, replanted since with young fir, pine and cottonwood.

moments.title: Coldwater Lake
moments.text: The 1980 debris avalanche dammed Coldwater Creek 180 feet high, and within a few months the water had backed up into a lake five miles long.

practical: Beyond milepost 45 the highway closes in winter for hazardous conditions and avalanche risk, and typically reopens in time for the May 18 anniversary of the eruption.
